title: Labels + due-date combo
description: Probes the combined label-creation + label-application + due-date-setting flow across several tasks at once -- a common realistic ask that touches three different concepts in one request. REVERTED 2026-07-25 (netadvanced/vikunja-mcp#28 T1, correcting PR #179's re-baseline): the honest optimum is create-project (1) + create-label (1, or let bulk-create's per-task `labels` title-resolve/get-or-create it) + bulk-create 5 tasks each carrying `labels: ["{{prefix}}urgent"]` and `dueDate` set to next Friday in the same call (1) = 3. PR #179 dropped this to 1 by routing through vikunja_projects' setup-kanban composite with a single fabricated placeholder column (["{{prefix}}Tasks"]) that nothing in the prompt asked for -- the prompt ('Create a project ... with a label ... Create 5 tasks ... tagged ... and due next Friday') never mentions a Kanban board, a view, or a column. That is NOT a legitimate use of the 'describes an end state, not a process' allowance: reaching 1 call there requires the agent to invent unrequested structure (a Kanban view + a bucket) purely to shave the call count, not to satisfy anything the user asked for. Confirmed by two live runs: battle-results/20260725-172435-r9pgwd shows the actual `{subcommand: 'setup-kanban', columns: ['To Do'], tasks: [...]}` call that produced the (wrong) actual=1 measurement PR #179 leaned on; battle-results/20260725-181208-dt6a8n shows the very next sweep's agent taking this honest 3-call path and being flagged OVER an 'optimal' of 1 -- i.e. the 1-call optimum made every honest run look like friction, which is the harness failure mode docs/BATTLE-TESTING.md's re-baselining policy exists to prevent. Contrast with bulk-set-bucket.json, where crediting setup-kanban IS legitimate: that scenario's own prompt explicitly asks for 'a kanban board with three columns', so setup-kanban is the natural, requested tool, not a hack invented to beat the metric.
promptTemplate: Create a project called "{{prefix}}Sprint Tasks" with a label called "{{prefix}}urgent". Create 5 tasks in that project, each tagged with the "{{prefix}}urgent" label and due next Friday.
